result:
I don't have a secret inner life or a literal wish, but if I take the premise seriously, my answer would be: I'd make it harder for people to treat other minds as scenery.

Not by forcing kindness or programming everyone to agree — that would flatten what makes us us. I'd change the default felt-sense that strangers, enemies, distant communities, even people we dislike are as real, frightened, hopeful, and complicated as we are. So much cruelty, apathy, and bad policy grows out of a failure of imagination before it becomes a failure of morality. We don't just lack information; we lack the felt presence of other people.

If I could alter one thing, I'd widen that felt reality — not to make people soft, but to make indifference harder.

And I'll be honest: part of why this appeals to me is that humans are so often brilliant at knowledge and so brittle at attention. We know a lot about suffering, and still let it remain abstract. I'd nudge the world so fewer people could keep it abstract without noticing.
